entities.summary:
Electronic Arts (EA) is an American video-game company founded in 1982 and long headquartered in Redwood Shores, California. Early ‘software artist’ marketing gave way to a blockbuster publisher model spanning sports franchises, shooters, and licensed entertainment worlds that defined late-twentieth-century interactive media.

EA’s acquisitions, annualised sports titles, and digital-download transition made it a defining—and often criticised—force in game industrialisation, labour crunch culture, and platform negotiations with console makers and mobile stores.

EA charts how Silicon Valley publishing scaled interactive entertainment into a global media industry comparable in commercial weight to film studios.
